name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 4, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 5:01
p.m., on May 4, 2009 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 29, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

At the hour of 5:03 p.m. Mayor Ury declared a recess to Closed Session. The City Council

City Council Minutes  1  May 4, 2009
 reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Mayor Pro Tem MacLean was
absent).

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission
  Viejo v. CUSD, Case No. 00180049; Companion Case, Rancho Santa Margarita v.
  CUSD, Case No. 00207543.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council received an update and provided direction
to staff and that there was no reportable action from Closed Session.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Introduction of Newly Appointed Chief of Police Lieutenant Mike Gavin

  Mayor Ury and City Manager Dennis Wilberg introduced Lieutenant Mike Gavin, newly
  appointed Chief of Police.

P2.  Certificate of Appreciation to the City of Mission Viejo for Support of Team Cody
  Projects for the Deployed Marines and Sailors of Camp Pendleton

  Mayor Ury received the Certificate of Appreciation and Flag from Staff Sergeant Stephen
  Ferguson.

P3.  Proclaim the Week of May 6 Through May 12, 2009, as National Nurses Week

  Mayor Ury presented the Proclamation to Linda Johnson, Vice President of Patient Care
  and Chief Nursing Officer at Mission Hospital.

P4.  2010 Census Kick Off

  Mayor Ury announced the City’s support of the United States Census Bureau’s efforts to
  help ensure a full and accurate count in 2010.

  Nadia Babayi, Partnership Specialist with the Bureau of the Census, U.S. Department of

City Council Minutes  2  May 4, 2009
   Commerce, provided additional information regarding current activities and opportunities
  for residents to get involved in the 2010 Census.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Neil Lonsinger, M.V.: stated that he was surprised to learn that the Montanoso Recreation Center
restroom remodel was estimated at $1 million and he hopes the City will not do the work at this
cost.

Michael Hay and Dinah Beattie, Board Members of the Mission Viejo High School Grad Nite
Corporation, M.V.: thanked the City Council, staff, and residents for helping to fund the 2009
Mission Viejo High School graduate celebration. Mr. Hay discussed the grad night activities and
encouraged residents to visit www.mvhsgradnite.com for more information.

Joe Holtzman, M.V.: stated that it is the fiduciary responsibility of the City Council and staff to
conduct an audit of Southern California Edison to assure that the City is receiving proper
revenue through the franchise agreement.

The following discussed ongoing problems with the construction activity at 26992 La Paja Lane:
Cathy Jasper, M.V.; Christine Saracino, M.V.; Richard Cordova, M.V.; and Stuart Jasper, M.V.
Mrs. Jasper presented a memo and pictures showing the status of the property as of May 1, 2009.
These residents asked the City to consider the statement of alleged shortcomings contained in the
memo.

Mayor Ury asked the Planning Department staff to provide a full response to the Jasper memo by
Friday, May 8, 2009, and to communicate that response to the City Council and the residents
involved.

Barbara Anderson, M.V.: discussed her attendance at Fun With Chalk and she thanked the City
for supporting this worthy event.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate
discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve
the Consent Calendar as outlined below.

City Council Minutes  3  May 4, 2009
 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  MacLean

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

3.  Check Register dated April 10, 2009, in the amount of $1,627,524.89

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated April 17, 2009, in the amount of $445,817.16

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  County of Orange City Aid Program Agreement for Fiscal Year 2009/2010

  Approved execution of Agreement No. D09-025 as required for participation in the
  County Proposition 42 City Aid Program.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Members Kelley and Schlicht requested corrections to the City Council Minutes
  to clarify an amended motion, correct the misspelling of a name, and to refine statements
  in each of their Council Comments.

City Council Minutes  4  May 4, 2009
   Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the
  Minutes for the City Council Meeting of April 20, 2009, as amended.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: MacLean

Council Member Schlicht requested that items 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12 be considered together.
She expressed concern with the recommendation to amend these contracts without going out to
bid to try and get a better price.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to approve
items 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12, as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, and Ury
NOES:  Schlicht
ABSENT:  MacLean

6.  Playground, Parkland, and Facilities Safety Inspection Services

  (1) Approved First Amendment to the existing contract with Jamey Clark, Inc. for the
  period July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2011, to increase the contract amount by an amount
  not to exceed $240,000.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase order to Jamey
  Clark, Inc. for the period July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2010, in an amount not to exceed
  $120,000.00.

8.  Graffiti Removal, Steam Cleaning, Painting, and Sealing Services Contract

  (1) Approved Third Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Bonanza
  Steam Cleaning, Inc. for the period July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2011, to increase the
  contract amount by an amount not to exceed $94,000.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue
  a purchase order to Bonanza Steam Cleaning, Inc. for the period July 1, 2009, through
  June 30, 2010, in an amount not to exceed $47,000.00.

9.  Annual Technical Irrigation Contract

City Council Minutes  5  May 4, 2009
   (1) Approved Second Amendment to the existing contract with A.C. Landscape, Inc. for
  the period July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2011, to increase the contract amount by an
  amount not to exceed $380,000.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase order to
  A.C. Landscape, Inc. for the period July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2010, in an amount not
  to exceed $190,000.00.

10.  Annual Routine Maintenance Program for Sidewalk Grinding

  (1) Approved Second Amendment to the existing contract with Channel Islands Sidewalk
  Grinding for the period July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2011, to increase the contract
  amount by an amount not to exceed $100,000.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a
  purchase order to Channel Islands Sidewalk Grinding for the period July 1, 2009, through
  June 30, 2010, in an amount not to exceed $ 50,000.00.

11.  Landscape and Irrigation Materials and Supplies Purchase Agreement -
  Hydroscape Products, Inc.

  (1) Approve the First Amendment to the existing contract with Hydroscape Products, Inc.
  for the period July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2011, to increase the contract amount by an
  amount not to exceed $236,000.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase order to
  Hydroscape Products, Inc. for the period July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2010, in an
  amount not to exceed $118,000.00.

12.  Landscape and Irrigation Materials and Supplies Purchase Agreement

  (1) Approved Third Amendment to the existing contract with John Deere Landscape,
  Inc. for the period July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2011, to increase the contract amount
  by an amount not to exceed $354,000.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase
  order to John Deere Landscapes, Inc. for the period July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2010,
  in an amount not to exceed $177,000.00.

7.  Orange County Regional Recycling and Waste Diversion Grant Program

  Senior Management Analyst Denise Matson presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht asked which South Orange County cities are applying for the
  grant and whether or not there is a budget for disbursement of the funds.

  Motion was made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Ury, to adopt
  Resolution 09-12 Approving Submittal of the Grant Application(s) and the Designation

City Council Minutes  6  May 4, 2009
   by Job Title of the Individual Authorized to Execute All Grant Documents on Behalf of
  the City of Mission Viejo.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: MacLean

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

13.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Received the report from Council Member Kelley.

14.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean was absent therefore there was no report on the
  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency.

15.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ledesma stated that there has not been a recent meeting of the San
  Joaquin Hills TCA.

16.  Roundabout Intersections Committee Report

  Bob Bruchmann, M.V.: expressed concern that the committee is focusing on the
  feasibility of a roundabout at Oso and Marguerite. He stated that several experts do not
  recommend this location and he objects to the request to hire Scott Ritchie to provide a
  report on this location because Mr. Ritchie has already determined that it is inadequate
  for a roundabout.

  Council Member Schlicht announced that City Manager Wilberg was to provide
  information to Scott Ritchie so he can explore a quick analysis and she will have a report
  at the next Council Meeting.

STAFF REPORTS

City Council Minutes  7  May 4, 2009
 City Manager’s Report

City Manager Dennis Wilberg announced that there is a special section on the City's web site
with daily updates on the swine flu, in particular the situation in the South County area. Mr.
Wilberg provided an update on his recent meeting with American Golf Association. He noted
that American Golf has indicated, once again, that they have no intention of selling the Casta del
Sol Golf Course. If it were for sale, it would only be sold for reuse as a golf course. Mr.
Wilberg stated that this information, coupled with the moratorium on the property, ensures that it
will continue as a golf course for the foreseeable future.

City Attorney's Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

17.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

Council Member Kelley

18.  Capital Improvement Projects

  Mayor Ury suggested that the projects be discussed separately.

  Due to difficult financial times, Council Member Kelley recommended that the
  Community Services Commission address the various elements being considered at the
  Marguerite Tennis Center so they can be broken down and addressed incrementally. She
  further recommended that the Pavion Park play equipment and Montanoso locker room
  projects be postponed.

  The following spoke in support of the Marguerite Tennis Center Improvements: Patti
  Bennett, M.V.; Wil Garcia, M.V.; Kime Goodrum, M.V.; and Tom Teichmann, M.V.

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma,
  to (1) defer the Montanoso Locker Room renovations and Pavion Park improvements and
  return the budgeted monies for those two projects to the City reserves; and (2) expedite

City Council Minutes  8  May 4, 2009
   and move forward with the Marguerite Tennis Center improvements as recommendations
  and a prioritized list of items come back from the Community Services Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: MacLean

Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance, on April 25th, at Artes de la Vida. She
commended staff and the volunteers for planning such a wonderful day. She was impressed with
the exhibits and entertainment, and she thanked the volunteers who came out to plant drought-
tolerant vegetation for the City. Council Member Kelley stated that these are the events that
make Mission Viejo stand out as a community where people want to live. Upon leaving Artes de
la Vida, she visited Lake Mission Viejo where four hundred of the City’s adopted Marines and
their families enjoyed a beautiful day at the lake. She thanked Dan Dobbs for the idea, Bruce
Hunt, Chairman of the Marine Adoption Committee for facilitating the event, along with the
volunteer members of the City’s Marine Adoption Committee. She also thanked the Albertsons
store at Olympiad Plaza for providing food and drinks and Dave Kerr, the Board Members, and
the staff at Lake Mission Viejo for generously opening their facility for our adopted Marines and
their families. Council Member Kelley displayed a Certificate of Appreciation that the City
received from the Headquarters Battalion for making “Mission Viejo Lake Day 2009” such a
great success. She also announced that she volunteered, this past weekend, at the Fun With
Chalk event. Council Member Kelley commended Dr. Frank Lieberman and his wife Elaine,
Norm Rosenkrantz, and the many volunteers on the Fun With Chalk Committee who came out to
help make this wonderful event possible. She encouraged those who could not attend this year to
mark their calendars and plan to attend next year. This is yet another unique event that makes
Mission Viejo special. Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character
word for the month of May is moral courage and she displayed the poster featuring a student
from Mission Viejo’s Newhart Middle School.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma recognized tennis enthusiast Wil Garcia for his persistence over the
years in requesting upgrades to the Marguerite Tennis Center. He stated that he was pleased to
attend the 11th annual Fun With Chalk festivities last weekend. It is a very special event and he
encouraged residents to come out next year. He also attended Santa Margarita Water District’s
Fiesta de Agua which is meant to teach young people about issues related to water. Council
Member Ledesma stated that it is great to represent the City at these functions.

City Council Minutes  9  May 4, 2009
 Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that she remembers resident Wil Garcia’s longtime request for a
single tennis court and she wishes the City could have moved faster on that. She inquired about
the Michael Chang Tennis Association bumping residents off of the courts and asked if we can
limit the associations’ time on the courts.

City Manager Wilberg responded that information was provided on that matter and staff will
redistribute the memo.

Council Member Schlicht stated that she is glad we are moving forward on the tennis centers
however she expressed concern that change orders are profit centers for contractors. She stated
that staff needs to do a better job with project oversight and monitoring the tax dollars that are
spent on these projects. She declared that we should have a recall every year because so far, the
City is saving over a million dollars, the golf course is safe and there will be no apartments over
the shops across the street. Council Member Schlicht announced that she had a great time at
Fun With Chalk. It is the City’s largest charitable event, the paintings are beautiful, and she is
constantly amazed at the dedication of the artists. She thanked the Holtzman Commission for
her notebook supply and commended the Mission Viejo Dispatch for a news report on the recent
capture of a parolee. It was another great job by our police officers and because the story did not
appear in the newspapers, she would not have been aware of it without the Mission Viejo
Dispatch story. Council Member Schlicht announced that Mission Viejo High School has two
stars: Mark Sanchez who was drafted for quarterback by the New York Jets and Nick Reed, who
has been drafted by the Seattle Seahawks. She also encouraged residents to go out and see the
local Orange County Gladiators, a pro basketball team. They are fun to watch and it is good
family entertainment. In relation to the outbreak of swine flu, Council Member Schlicht outlined
the Vector Control District’s three easy tips for preventing the spread of germs.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

Mayor Ury

19.  Oso Creek Improvements

  Motion was made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to direct the
  Community Services Commission to review the Oso Creek Improvement plans, both
  from a design standpoint and a financial standpoint, and report their findings back to the
  City Council prior to commencing with the proposed plans.

City Council Minutes  10  May 4, 2009
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: MacLean

20.  Support for SB 295

  Motion was made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to send a letter
  of support for SB 295 to Assemblyman Jeff Miller and the Senate Environmental Quality
  Committee.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: MacLean

Mayor Ury announced that he too attended Artes de la Vida. It was a wonderful event and it was
great to see all the people come out that day. He also attended Fun With Chalk and he
congratulated Dr. Lieberman and the volunteers who make it such an outstanding event. Mayor
Ury thanked all of the City’s volunteers and staff members who participate to make these events
possible.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:24 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, May 18, 2009, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 18, 2009

City Council Minutes  11  May 4, 2009
